clue.text: Where deal might be made with noted philosopher

parts.note: to have noted something is to have seen it, so noted gives saw
John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher

explanation.surface: A business agreement struck in the company of a famous thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is not a business agreement here: it is deal wood, pine or fir planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood timber, and a mill that saws logs into planks is where such timber is produced.

clue.text: Wise to limit commute with no second-class adult fare

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose or bound, so the word for wise goes around the rest

parts.note: a sage is wise

indicators.note: with no means without, so this letter is removed

parts.note: to commute is to travel to work, which you might bus
B is a second-class grade
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: Wise travellers cut costs by avoiding second-class adult tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food, and a banger is one example of everyday food.

clue.text: Descriptive statistic revised where data give incomplete information

indicators.note: revised means altered, so these letters are rearranged
incomplete means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A statistic changed where the data only partly informs.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN, slang for information, loses its last letter to give GE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean in which each value counts according to its importance is a summary measure of data.

clue.text: Liberal abandons best conceivable plan

indicators.note: abandons means leaves, so this letter goes out of the word

parts.note: ideal means the best that can be imagined

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician gives up on the best possible plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea in the sense of a scheme or intention is a plan for doing something.

clue.text: Period drama regularly featuring upper-class oppressed by desire

indicators.note: in a down answer, being oppressed by means lying beneath, so the desire comes first

parts.note: lust is strong desire

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the letters hold the abbreviation inside
regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A period drama where the upper classes are crushed by desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period drama' looks like one phrase, but 'Period' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-year span, from the Roman purification held every five years, is a period of time.

clue.text: This part of plant receives orders to supply special delivery

indicators.note: the letters are ordered, put in a new arrangement, to produce the answer once the named letters are taken out

parts.note: these letters are the ones removed from the fodder before rearranging

explanation.surface: A plant takes in instructions to arrange an express parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of RECEIVES out of SPECIAL DELIVERY; the seven left over, P A L D L I Y, are rearranged to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is the broad floating leaf of a water lily, so it is one part of that aquatic plant.

clue.text: Dance during Christmas period mainly served up music unsuitable for the occasion

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means presented upwards, so the letters read backwards
during means within, so the dance goes inside
mainly means most of, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Yule is the Christmas season
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone serves up music unfit for a dance held at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' is a reversal signal for a down clue, and 'during' places the dance inside the shortened Christmas word before the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing song to send babies to sleep would be wrong music for a lively Christmas ball.

clue.text: Butcher's left with no pork every so often

definitions.note: rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so a butcher's is a look

indicators.note: every so often means at regular intervals, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A butcher left without pork now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang, 'butcher's hook' for look, as in 'have a butcher's'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a butcher's is a glance, so the noun means a glance or peek.

clue.text: Shoe shop starts to rile customers, foolishly charging money for shine

indicators.note: foolishly means in a silly way, so all these letters are rearranged
starts are first letters, one from each word

parts.note: pence are British coins, so money

explanation.surface: A shoe shop annoys customers by stupidly charging for a polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' links the money to the pool: the shop letters, R and C, and PENCE all go into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a faint glow given off by some substances, so it is a kind of shine.

clue.text: Leaves off sides and tops of small trees are variegated

indicators.note: variegated means made varied, so the letters are mixed up
in a down answer, tops are first letters

explanation.surface: A description of mottled leaves on the edges and crowns of small trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage, fitting the trees, but 'Leaves off' is a verb meaning stops.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave off doing something is to stop or cease, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Their vital bank contributions are well received by everyone

definitions.text: Their vital bank contributions are well received by everyone

parts.words: Their vital bank contributions are well received by everyone
parts.note: the bank is a blood bank, and the contributions are blood donations that any patient's body accepts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but the vital contributions are blood: type O negative blood can be given to patients of any blood group.
explanation.definitionFit: People with blood group O negative give blood that any recipient can safely take, hence the medical name for them.

clue.text: Some teachers could be a pain in the neck

definitions.text: could be a pain in the neck

indicators.note: Some says only part of the following word is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A jibe that certain teachers can be really annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pain in the neck' reads as the idiom for an annoying person, but here it is literal: a sore neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent physical hurt felt in the neck is one example of this kind of pain.

clue.text: Fantastic American piece about cuts

indicators.note: cuts means goes into, so the word for about is placed inside the gun

parts.note: a gat is American slang for a gun, which is also called a piece
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Praise for a terrific American artwork about reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms of strong approval, meaning wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Copies part of church running east west

indicators.note: running means moving, so one letter shifts its position in the word
west means towards the left, so the letter moves leftwards in the across word

parts.note: an apse is the vaulted recess at the end of a church
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A section of a church building that faces in an unexpected direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Churches traditionally have the apse at the east end; here the E itself goes west, one place left.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, so the verb means copies or mimics.

clue.text: Some growth in knowledge is deliberate

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Learning grows somewhat on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate as a verb means to ponder or consider carefully, the same as the answer.

clue.text: IKEA rotated 50 lines with identical features

indicators.note: rotated means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50, and also the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Flat-pack furniture spun through fifty lines all looking the same.
explanation.walkthrough: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain; its letters are turned around with L, the Roman fifty, among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are similar in every respect look the same, so they resemble each other.

clue.text: Town square briefly quiet in the morning

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to be square is to be even, owing nothing either way
sh is the call for quiet
a.m. is the abbreviation for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A town square that is briefly peaceful early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the name of a particular English market town, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Range of colours sure to include trace of light blue

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the word for sure goes around the rest

parts.note: yes and sure are both ways to agree

indicators.note: a trace is a tiny amount, here just the first letter

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling low or down

explanation.surface: A paint range that definitely contains a hint of pale blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light blue' looks like one colour, but 'light' supplies a letter and 'blue' means a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural covers the many shades of one hue, from lemon to mustard, forming a range of colours.

clue.text: Like recycled tin cans?

indicators.note: recycled means made into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what used tin cans are like.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the cans are tin, and their letters are recycled.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemistry adjective means relating to or containing tin, from the Latin stannum for that metal.

clue.text: Felt contempt for Sun's top journalist ringing my number

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the outer letters surround the rest
in a down answer, the top is the first letter

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for an editor
cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A tabloid's senior journalist phoning a number they look down on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which suits the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to regard them with disdain, so the past tense means felt disdain.

clue.text: Feature controlling opening of gate on elevated section of locks

indicators.note: controlling means holding, so the feature contains the letter

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: the opening is the first letter

explanation.surface: A mechanism that operates a gate on a raised stretch of canal locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' and 'gate' suggest a canal, but the locks are hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot or coil of hair pinned up at the back of the head is a raised arrangement of tresses.

clue.text: Yahoo admits leak damaged growth of branch

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the oaf holds the rest inside

parts.note: a yahoo is a boor or lout, as is an oaf

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lout confesses that a damaged leak came from a company branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage of this tree sprouts from its twigs and boughs, so it is something a branch grows.

clue.text: Exam containing new papers returned first, perhaps

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the exam goes around the rest

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read the other way

parts.note: ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: An exam with new papers given back first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: first is one such number.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers like first, second and third mark position in a series, so first is an example.

clue.text: Illicit reproduction beneficial to heartless upper classes

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of or good for it

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the central letters go

parts.note: the gentry are the people of high social class

explanation.surface: An unlawful copy that suits the uncaring upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fake made to pass as genuine, such as a counterfeit painting, is an unlawful copy.

clue.text: Frank not to start competition anyone can enter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ajar, as a door that is not shut to
third meaning: to begin or launch
fourth meaning: a contest without entry restrictions, as in golf

explanation.walkthrough: Four meanings in a row. 'Not to' means the opposite of shut to, as a door is pushed to, so not to is ajar.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word serves as adjective for candid and ajar, verb for begin, and noun for a tournament with no qualification.

clue.text: Objects to attitude ignoring terms of fine print

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a mindset is a fixed attitude

indicators.note: terms are ends, here the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone resents an attitude that disregards the small print of a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'fine' and 'print', E and T, are removed from MINDSET.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone minds something they dislike it and raise an objection to it.

clue.text: Award initially overlooked evidence of harm

indicators.note: the first letter is passed over and so left out

parts.note: an Oscar is the Academy Award for film

explanation.surface: An award first snubbed leaves its mark on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on skin after a wound has healed shows that an injury once happened.

clue.text: Cistern smelt awful without lid

indicators.note: in a down answer, the lid is the top letter, so it is removed

parts.note: stank means smelt bad

explanation.surface: A water tank that reeked badly because its lid was off.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a container for storing water, which is a kind of water container.

clue.text: Return blows

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the letters read the other way

parts.note: raps are sharp blows

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit back.
explanation.walkthrough: In the whole clue, boxers swap punches; in the wordplay, RAPS goes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, trading punches with a partner, so returning punches.

clue.text: Mean, idiotic church banning one entertaining writer, almost

parts.note: near is an old-fashioned word for mean or stingy

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the idiotic church holds the writer between its parts
banning means excluding, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: asinine means stupid, like a donkey
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: A stingy, foolish church that nearly shuts out a guest author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' for mean (stingy) is an old usage. The phrase is British slang for very nearly, ninepence being old pre-decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means virtually or very nearly, just as this word does.

clue.text: Hide writing table belonging to old dons

indicators.note: dons means puts on and wears, so the letters wear the abbreviation inside them

parts.note: a desk is a writing table
in can mean belonging to, as in a member in a club

explanation.surface: A desk owned by elderly university teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university fellows, but it is the verb meaning wears.
explanation.definitionFit: The leather made from the skin of a female deer is a hide, here a noun for an animal's skin.

clue.text: Treatment of allergy for the majority

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over, giving a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Allergy care being given to most patients.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means mostly or to a great extent, describing most of something.
